submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE was 0.0162% at index 18 (Cr 0.37 / Sb 0.63). EQE rose steadily with Sb content across the three measurements: 0.0017% at Cr 0.69, 0.0045% at Cr 0.51 and 0.0162% at Cr 0.37. This fits an Sb-rich rutile/trirutile phase working best.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0017%; the Cr-rich side performs worst

consultations.verdict: Support: CrSbO4 (rutile-type, Cr:Sb 1:1) predicted HSE gap ~2.0 eV < 2.7 eV photon energy, and near-stable (0.065 eV/atom above hull). Index 13 (Cr 0.51) is closest to 1:1 stoichiometry, a good first probe.

Support: Cr-rich Cr5Sb3O16 predicted gap ~2.0 eV (absorbs at 2.7 eV). Sb-rich CrSb2O6 has a 0.96 eV prediction, which may mean metallic-like losses, so it is less favoured. Probing the Cr-rich side at index 7 (Cr 0.69).

Mildly against / uninformative: the Cr3Sb5O16 ordered cell's predicted gap is 0.88 eV. The measured trend goes the other way, though: EQE rises from Cr 0.69 to Cr 0.51. Real films are likely a rutile solid solution, not this ordered cell. So I am testing the Sb-rich side at index 18 (Cr 0.37).
